string.text: {=eyxfHmCU}I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}, of the {CLAN_NAME}. Our family has served the Vlandian people for generations.
{=FFXqPFwl}I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}, of the {CLAN_NAME}, one of the most illustrious families in the annals of the Vlandian people.

{=a8584KD0}I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}, of the {CLAN_NAME}. I am sure you have heard the name of our clan in the epics of the steppe. We carry the name of one the 12 sons of the great she-wolf, mother of the Khuzait.
{=z2yr4mc6}I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}, of the {CLAN_NAME}. Our clan has loyally served the Khuzait for generations.
{=267ch9fZ}That raid on {VILLAGE_NAME}... Hard on the farmers there. Well, anyway, I'm sure the {ENEMY_NAME} would have done the same to our us.

{=ZPaw3WuO}The Vlandians are the descendants of mercenaries from the west who served the Empire for many centuries. Famed across Calradia for their mounted warriors who fight with spears and lances on horseback, they served loyally, but secretly yearned for a time when they could break from imperial rule and govern themselves. In recent years, they have formed an independent kingdom led by a caste of warlike nobles.

{=c1Ag8YJS}The Battanians still remember the olden days when the woods stretched across northern Calradia, and the Empire and its cities had yet to violate their sanctity. The fierce warriors remain loyal to their traditional ways. They paint their faces when going to battle and even their noblemen prefer to fight on foot while using great axes and two-handed swords with deadly efficiency.

{=HkZ4E94O}The tribes of the Khuzait live a largely nomadic life, riding from their settlements in the Devseg Plateau to raid and trade with neighbouring lands. Despite having permanent camps, they still retain many aspects of their nomadic life, including their affinity with horses. They are masters of mounted archery, shooting and then galloping out of reach.

{=HD2wzAxz}Sturgians are the descendants of the foreign tribes of northern Calradia. As the empire expanded into their cold forests, they found a ready market for the luxurious furs of woodland animals whom they traditionally hunted and trapped. Sturgian chieftains became princes, vying for pre-eminence with the help of Nord mercenaries who migrated into their realm. They are good hunters and wanderers, travelling far in search of opportunities both for trade and for plunder.

{=Khr5yETv}The Aserai are the inhabitants of the Nahasa desert, a mixture of nomadic bedouin and settled oasis farmers. They are famous for their horsemanship and their knowledge of the learning of many lands, especially medicine, gained from lying on some of the continent's most lucrative trade routes. Each clan is fiercely proud of its lineage and often jealous of the others, but when united by a charismatic leader, they become a major force in the south.

{=bj0Ko5uX}The Calradian Empire is in crisis. Political rivalries have torn the land in three, with claimants attempting to seize power for themselves, whilst enemies close on all sides, carving new kingdoms from imperial territory. They are technologically more advanced than their neighbors and their mastery of engineering is not just evident in their aqueducts, beautiful architecture and massive city walls. It also makes them experts in siege warfare.
{=1PwQxaOu}Preparations seem to be under way for a tournament. Prize is {ITEM}.
{=8bSHlWBL}There is no tournament currently in this town.

{=str.str_culture_description.massa}The Massa are a hardy migrant people from the lands of Jumne. Like their Vlandian cousins, they are famed across Calradia as stalwart mercenaries and masters of horse, axe and lance, serving across the continent in the myriad wars of the Calradian Empire. Recently, they have declared themselves an independent kingdom, conquering one of the Empire's rich north-western provinces.

{=str.str_culture_description.gotarni}The Gotarnians are a remnant of the once-proud Myzean people, a Palaic tribal group from north-eastern Calradia. They are a brutal society, tempered by centuries of constant warfare, though also not unaccustomed to urban life, building great cities on the verdant eastern plains. Their warriors are known as great riders, and feared for their use of the deadly falx.

{=str.str_culture_description.cizygian}The tribes of the Cizygians are a recent arrival in Calradia, having descended from the eastern Calradian Steppe within living memory. A formidable nomadic people, those from the court of the Darshi Padishah to the halls of Vlandia speak in hushed whispers of their vast hordes galloping across the plains. Like their Khuzait cousins, they are masters of mounted archery, shooting and then galloping out of reach.

{=str.str_culture_description.vakken}The Vakken are the original inhabitants of northern Calradia. Conquered many years ago by the Calradian Empire, they have modelled much of their society in the imperial fashion, founding colonies along the northern coasts of Lake Laconis, and warring with the neighbouring Sturgians. In battle, their legions are not unlike those of the Empire, wielding swords, javelins and shields.

{=str.str_culture_description.darshi}The Darshi are the inhabitants of a vast empire to the east and south of Calradia, ruled over by an ancient lineage of Padishahs. Whilst in Calradia they are referred to as a single group, the Darshi are in fact a series of smaller satrapies, each with their own unique culture and leaders. In battle, they are known for their robust infantry and powerful shock cavalry.

{=str.str_culture_description.shariz}The Kannic people are the ancient inhabitants of coastal regions of the western Nahasa desert. From their capital at Quyaz, they once ruled over a vast empire. However, they were conquered centuries ago by the Calradian Empire, forming the southernmost of its provinces. Recently independent, they now vie for control of the Nahasa, sending their legions against both their former Calradian rulers and Aserai neighbours.

{=str.str_culture_description.empire_n}The Calradian Empire is in crisis. Political rivalries have torn the land in three, with claimants attempting to seize power for themselves, whilst enemies close on all sides, carving new kingdoms from imperial territory. They are technologically more advanced than their neighbors and their mastery of engineering is not just evident in their aqueducts, beautiful architecture and massive city walls. It also makes them experts in siege warfare.

{=QpBmbygb}Know of the Diamond Guild? Then maybe you've heard that the Empire rid of us because were too warlike. Rubbish- everyone knows they cast us out because we were winning all their wars for them and making their legions look weak. So don't try anything rash.

{=ge3FF3dd}I'm tired of explaining ourselves to strangers, so I'll tell you this much. It doesn't matter if we're Khuzait, Aserai, Calradian or- heavens forbid, Vlandian- we can ride as well as any nomad! I'll be happy to demonstrate if you don't believe me.

{=0pt1m4t3}The Calradoi may take many things from us, but so long as the Venatio live on they will never take our legacy. Though, I don't imagine you are here to learn about our glorious people... are you?
{=7jyjyjyjyjyjyrr}A lonely soul. But there is more to it.
{=6ueghregg}I am a desert guide. Without me, the hots sands will claim you. I know all the oases, all the canyons and everything else beyond the horizon.

{=fELWdbuL}More than just the heat, I also protect travelers from other dangers. Whether they be nasty pests like vipers and scorpions or even sandstorms, I make sure they reach their destinations. And I won't be found rummaging your bags either- you have my word that your goods will be safe too.
{=u4hhhfdffdfd}The name's {MET_WANDERER.FIRSTNAME}, a simple finder of oases and your most valuable companion in the desert... unlike that other wastrel. That one talks too much.
{=aa33543ggd}Just {MET_WANDERER.FIRSTNAME} works. So, what brings you here?
{=trg44g}A Jawwal then. Your kind are barely more valuable than sand.

{=y6878864gf}My... bretheren do not look kindly on me, nor any travelers. And with all this war going on, there just isn't enough protection against them. And as an outcast of outcasts, I must say that it has become quite lonely.
{=ser3341}Make no mistake though, I can handle myself in a fight. Oh and I'm sure you will find use for my scouting skills.
{=EMkaeD9M}Its an unhappy story, but perhaps it will make you feel better about your luck.

{=RaSZtTqh}I was the son of a slave. My master raised me in his house, but it was clear that he wasn't interested in my sucess. Still, I was educated with his other sons, and while they got all the attention I made up for it with focus. I thought once I was freed, I could be a merchant.

{=9AIyvTmF}I thank my father for making sure that even in death, the debt that he left me was small. But alas, I had nothing else. As it turns out, a merchant starting out in the world must either have a great deal of money, or connections to leverage. I had neither, but I would not let that stop me. No, I took work as a hired hand, guarding a caravan.

{=ZuHolx2r}Now I will not say it to their faces, but my old master’s brats toughened me up good. Life on the road was no fun, but at least I was hardened and could handle myself in a fight. The Caravan Master took a liking to me, he said I should lead my own caravan one day. And so that became my goal.
{=A9r6SnWx}You've done alright for yourself. But what now?
{=B7cMisFf}Then why are you wasting away here?

{=HaQlEZPq}A Jawwal ambush has set my plans back a little. Yes, I've not much friends, gold or dignity left, but at least I am alive. Perhaps if I were to join a more capable party, I could try again.

{=vgcTdEvc}I was the son of a slave, but my father bought me my freedom. I came from nothing, but I can only grow from here. Times are tough now, but they are tough for everyone. Perhaps I can benefit from joining the war rather than enduring it.

{=xNPAZdtX}My father is Aytham, son of Thamuq, who was son of Munbilas - the elder son, mind you, not the younger - and he was son of Numayn - Numayn of the Mountain, that is, not the less illustrious ones of that name - and he was son of Zais.

{=ikWAfIHX}Now some people will tell you that Zais was born of out wedlock, but those are lies. He was the legitimate son of Ghutan, and Rasad 'Ban Ghutan' doesn't deserve that name, he should be called the 'Bastard,' not Zais. Anyway, as for Ghutan's father... Well, not everyone knows this, but...
{=Wz71n66t}I'm sorry. Are you not paying attention?
{=N9rVRfaW}Oh.. Of course I am! This is fascinating. But tell me about your own ventures.
{=SYBe3aIC}Do you have a trade? Any skills? Or just a string of ancestors?

{=KGa4gmDW}Ah, yes. See, as inheritor of such legacy I have made myself excellent with denars. My enterprises were so successful that I became known as 'the Golden', see? But alas, war has devastated my businesses. So, I work for those who pay me my value in denars, good noble denars.

{=vKSGJNxT}I am a merchant, and a fine one. I would recite to you my lineage, but that would take an hour. I would tell you my ventures, but that would take two. So, instead - if you pay me - I shall come with you and manage your logistics, your business and your denars. Then you will know why they call me the Golden.
{=5geffd4222}I suppose I will. Judge me as you wish, but I am proud of who I am.

{=ee2j5yff}My father is from one of the great clans, but to name him would scandalise him. He is not a terrible man, but alas my mother proved to be his weakness... one that he would at least try to make up for in secret. We looked after well enough in his household, even as simple servants.

{=142fffefefef}My 'real' father however? Now he was a disgrace and bless my mother but she chose poorly. Its a miracle anyone would think that I ever came from that oath, and the more I grew, the more I took after my real father's noble heritage. It did not hurt that I inherited his prowess either.

{=k6fvy5}Well my supposed father is many things, but he is not foolish. He figured out quick. He threatened to expose it, to ruin the clan and I... well after the blood was cleaned I had no choice but to flee. Perhaps one day I can return as a newly made woman.
{=43hhthth}Such a messy affair, and not any fault of your own.
{=mi76u633}The lies of nobilty is not worth murdering over.
{=bhhyn774}At any rate, I will find a master who allows me to win fame for myself. Perhaps I can then make a new name for myself.
{=6yne4t4t}I am but a common warrior, of a great clans I mustn't name. I do not need that name, only to prove it with deeds for a worthy master.
{=rgSWtZ0w}Well I have nothing better to do, and seems you don't either. So listen...

{=ZSaGzgmN}I was a slave soldier in training. No, not one of Unqid's new Mamelukes, but the old order. Back then, warrior slaves were heavy infantry, and we were damned good at it. Could have given the Calradian Legionaries a real fight I reckon! But we were rendered obsolete before that.

{=cyjb9lmm}When Unqid came into power, he did so with eastern slaves trained in horse archery. To him, elite slave infantry was a thing of the past, daresay it was never truly the Aserai way. Slave soldiers like us only ever happened because none of the Aseri were willing to slog it out on foot. Why waste themselves when they could use slaves instead?

{=PKzUUVKC}But besides all that, Unqid had to remove us because we had become too influential. Quite a few of us had become lords as a matter of fact. Unqid couldn't have that for his new Sultanate. But if you ask me, if his Mamelukes are half the men we were, they'll be no less ambitious. Oh they may be his loyal dogs now, but it won't be long before Unqid's grandchildren have to deal with a Mameluke Sultanate.
{=gMiceyRl}Quite unfortunate to be denied a future not once, but twice.
{=KrXlrnsg}The quarries are hiring. If you're not up for banditry, then that might be all you're good for.

{=XKsjweaA}I was made to be a soldier. There is no fun in being a rich fool's bodyguard or booting rowdy drunks from stinky taverns. But you know what? At least I am free... free to choose another master anyway.
{=wQRSM1lz}I can fight well, and I've some learning too. Us slave warriors hadn't much of a life besides training. Take me in and I'll more than earn my keep.

{=awe222yyyr}I am not a smart nor a charming lass. But I am big and strong. Big and strong enough to beat heads in and keep the prisoners in line. The Hippo they called me, and I wear that name with pride- nothing scarier in the South than a Hippo I tell you!

{=575h4hh4e}Yeah, I was a slaver. Couldn't exactly whore myself out, and I was not born to a good family. There was nothing much I could do. I didn't go out of my way to push no one into slavery either, I simply guarded the goods is all. I'm no monster, so yeah I had some pity. But you get used to it.

{=t4trr3r3}... at least that's what I tell myself. Do I give a damn about debtors, crooks and the war prisoners? Nah, they risked it and so their misfortune is their's. But the women and children? I've always had a soft spot for them. Never is fair when gotta suffer for the failings of the men you know?
{=mk6u54}I suppose you weren't a complete villain then.
{=22refuuu76u6}Too bad you weren't decent enough to leave the slave trade.

{=ke4hc}No, but I had enough when some of the slavers started taking... 'liberties' with some of the children. That was more than enough for me to remind them why they called me the Hippo... needless to say my boss was not too happy.
{=t4jvvrrtt4}I can fight well, and I reckon I have a decent handle of trade. Take me in and I'll more than earn my keep.

{=n4ggdh77}Hmm. Many men would begin their story by reciting their ancestry. I will not do this. A man should be judged on his own deeds, and a long list of ancestors does him no credit. Also, my family does not acknowledge me, so why should I acknowledge them?

{=5gem6}I was a vagrant wastrel. A disgrace to my poor family, a man with no hope to his life. I begged, mugged and looted my way through life, barely alive. As far as everyone could care, I was doomed. Everyone except one holy man.

{=gdrrrgu766}He took me into his monastery, and had me cleaned up. Gave me a room, fed me. All this in exchange for cleaning up their place. A crook like me deserved none of it, but I'll be damned if I didn't try my best to live well. Before long, they had me helping out with the healing. Turned out to be my true calling, and just like that they taught me how to tend to the wounded.

{=mnn5t4gfdu89}Alas, these things were not to last. A band of Khuzait raiders stormed the monastery and killed all the monks including my dear master. I was made of harder stuff, but not so hard as to save them all. So its much to my shame that I alone survived. A vagrant like me.
{=3fefe5578}A reminder of what a terrible world we live in.
{=997gff4}I hope you haven't relasped into old habits.

{=a48ggr45}I ask myself why I, out of all of them survived. It drives me mad at times... but I've chosen to live on in their memory. Make something of myself... even if its joining up in war as a surgeon.
{=563gfff343}I was vagrant given a chance to make something of myself. I offer my skills to war-leaders, who need the skills of hardy surgeons.
{=m4y5y22ee2e2}I'm not that interesting, so forgive my tale...

{=1fff4j}I was a respected surgeon in an army's camp train, while the love of my life was a rising hero. Our love was no small one and doubtless the camp tired of us! But I save many soldiers, and he would kill many more. But I never resented that, he was a brave and wonderful man. I thought he would be mine, but alas, he was already devoted to another.

{=y5yymm}There was one battle we were not doing so well in, so my lover was ordered out of the camp to bolster the front. When he left, a band of enemy raiders swooped in to try divert him back and keep him from tipping the scales. I could remember watching as agonised over the choice to make- to save us, or turn the tides of the greater battle to save his liege. Well he chose well and now they sing of his deeds.

{=j3aa3}The terrible cost was not unknown to anyone that listen to his legend, but many would agree that it saved our lands and many more people. Even I can agree... but damn it's hard to accept. Can you honestly tell those poor camp followers that their sacrifice was necessary?
{=234rr33}It is no easy choice to make, weighing the value of life is a cruel thing.
{=1urth44}A few whores and cooks are a small price to pay for honour and glory.

{=4117jyjyj}Sometimes I wonder if he misses me. A part of me hopes that he does, and that he regrets that choice. But another part hates that I miss him anyway. So I give my services as an army surgeon, one that you can leave undefended if you must.
{=u6320y5yes}I am known as a tragic sacrifice. I am the helper of the forgotten, the lost and the weak. But for you, I am an able surgeon and a hardened woman.
